charlie_customer: Hey team — our private inference cluster in prod (vpc-abc123) started failing for some customers around 08:32 UTC. Clients see streaming TCP resets during TLS handshake, downstream errors like "connection reset by peer" and spikes in failed requests. No recent deploys on our side.

alice_support: Sorry about that, can you paste a recent failing request id and client error? Also, which subnet/NAT path are they using?

charlie_customer: Request id 01F9Z1-req-9b. Affected traffic from us-east-1 private subnets -> nat-a -> IGW. Failing for about 12% of requests, intermittent. Logs show TLS alert 40 (handshake failure) and then RST.

alice_support: Thanks. First suspicion: asymmetric return path or NACL/SG blocking ephemeral return ports. Quick checks: 1) can you tcpdump on the instance when reproing? 2) confirm your subnet NACL rules (both in and out) include ephemeral port range.

charlie_customer: Running tcpdump now. Sample capture shows client SYN -> SYN-ACK -> then server sends FIN+RST during handshake. Paste of tcpdump snippet:

```
08:32:15.123456 IP client.51234 > instance.443: Flags [S], seq 0
08:32:15.123457 IP instance.443 > client.51234: Flags [S.], seq 0 ack 1
08:32:15.124000 IP instance.443 > client.51234: Flags [R], seq 1
```

charlie_customer: NACL inbound/outbound both have explicit ALLOW for 443, but I see deny entries for ranges that might overlap ephemeral ports (we have a DENY 49152-65535 in the outbound list for some reason).

alice_support: That DENY on 49152-65535 is suspicious. Linux ephemeral port range often is 32768-60999 depending on distro. If outbound NACL blocks the client's source port range, replies will be dropped and connection torn down. Can you temporarily remove that DENY and retest?

bob_infra: Also check security group egress on the instance role. SGs are stateful so typically okay, but NACLs are stateless and must allow both directions for the port ranges in use.

charlie_customer: I removed the DENY on 49152-65535 and re-tested — error rate dropped to ~0.5% during the same load. Will keep running for another 30m.

alice_support: Nice, that points to NACL ephemeral blocking. For a robust fix we recommend: 1) update NACL to allow ephemeral range used by your OS (check `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range`). 2) audit any DENY rules that precede the allow (NACLs evaluate by rule number). 3) consider using a NAT Gateway instead of one-off NAT instances to reduce odd translation behaviour.

charlie_customer: My `/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range` is `32768    60999`. We have a business rule that added DENY 49152-65535 to the NACL earlier. Looks like it overlapped.

alice_support: Exactly. Two follow-ups to prevent regression: - Add a monitoring check for TLS handshake failure rate spikes on the private subnet. - Add a terraform guard to prevent NACL denies that overlap ip_local_port_range.

dave_sre: tagging for visibility. Also check conntrack table saturation on the NAT host: `sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count` and `nf_conntrack_max`. If conntrack wraps you can see unexpected RSTs. Example sysctl to increase: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` and tune `tcp_timeout_established`.

charlie_customer: conntrack_count was 230k, nf_conntrack_max 262144. No wrap yet but good to know. We'll increase to 400k while we ramp.

alice_support: Great. If you prefer, I can open an escalation to eng-sre to review NAT/conntrack & NACL rule evolution. Deploy-bot will also post any recent infra changes.

deploy-bot: infra-change: NAT instance terraform apply by infra-team at 2026-03-15T07:41:02Z — added NACL deny rule 100 (49152-65535) intended to limit outbound ephemeral range for compliance.

dave_sre: Looks like a policy change introduced the deny. Recommend rollback and coordinate a compliant approach (e.g., allow ports but restrict destinations). I'll set a short incident runbook item to verify all private subnets.

charlie_customer: Rolling back DENY fully now and increasing conntrack. Will update in ~15m with metrics. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

alice_support: Thanks — please paste the post-change success metrics when available. If things regress we'll capture pcap + `aws ec2 describe-network-acls` output and escalate further.

charlie_customer: Update 08:54 UTC — error rate dropped to 0.2% after rollback and conntrack bump. Marking this as resolved for now, will follow up with infra on a permanent rule change.

alice_support: Awesome, closing loop. Suggested permanent fix in ticket: allow ip_local_port_range on NACL or move to NAT Gateway + stricter destination-level controls.

charlie_customer: Filing internal RFC to avoid future DENY overlapping ephemeral ranges. Thanks all.
